summary.text: 名 is currently written with 口 on the left and 夕 on the right. The received traditional account treats both as semantic elements: evening 夕 and speaking-related 口 evoke identifying oneself by calling out a name in darkness, though this does not establish the graph’s original motivation.

formation.text: The graph’s current form places 口 on the left and 夕 on the right. The received analysis treats both as semantic elements: 夕 supplies the evening setting and 口 the speaking/name idea in the account of identifying oneself in darkness. A secondary proposal assigns 夕 a phonetic role, but it remains unverified; the original motivation is unresolved.

components.text: 夕 is the right-hand element. In the received explanation of 名, it supplies the evening setting. Separately, 夕 and 月 once shared a moon-like form; their later graphic differentiation belongs to their own histories, not a change within 名.

口 is the left-hand element. In the received explanation, it contributes the speaking/name idea as a semantic element. The cited accounts identify it in 名 but do not describe a separate graphic history for it within this character.

history.text: 名 is recorded in oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, small-seal, and Shuowen forms. The selected oracle-style and Western Zhou bronze-style images are modern vector drawings of forms associated with 名; they show different examples, not a proven sequence of graphic change.

The night-identification account appears in the Shuowen explanation and is repeated in later descriptions. A competing proposal says 口 may once have written both 口 and 名, with 夕 added as a sound indicator associated with a graph later written 明. This proposal remains unverified, and the cited reconstructions do not support 夕 as a phonetic for 名.
A rare added-stroke form found on a stele is described as an unusual variant resembling an error, not as an ancestral form.

uncertainties.text: The traditional explanation relates the graph to 夕 and 口, but does not independently establish the original motivation. The proposed phonetic role for 夕 and its suggested connection with a graph later written 明 remain unverified.
The earliest cited oracle-bone token occurs in a place name; its date and interpretation are unresolved, and it is not an unambiguous ordinary use meaning “name.”
The cited uses and dictionary senses do not establish when personal-name, naming, inscription, reputation, or status meanings first arose, or a continuous path among them.

senses.text: The earliest cited use is a token in a place name; its precise interpretation is unresolved.

senses.period: Western Zhou bronze and Warring States manuscripts
senses.text: A Western Zhou inscription uses 名 as a verb meaning “name” or “designate”; Warring States manuscripts also attest name or designation uses. These examples do not establish when the sense first arose.
One bronze use is glossed as 銘, “inscription.” The evidence does not resolve whether this is a meaning development or 名 used to write a related word.
名 is used for a person’s name, though the cited material does not date the first occurrence of this sense.
名 also means to name or designate; the evidence does not establish its chronology relative to the noun sense.
Dictionary sources list reputation and status-related meanings, but do not establish when they arose or how they developed.

limitations.text: The earliest cited token is a place name, not an unambiguous use for an ordinary personal name. The available examples do not establish first dates or semantic links among the other senses.
The bronze use glossed as 銘 does not establish a development from “name” to “inscription”; it may represent 名 used to write a related word, but the relationship is unresolved.

overview.text: 名 means “name” or “to name.” Its current form has 口 on the left and 夕 on the right. The traditional account treats both as semantic elements in identifying oneself by calling out in darkness; its original motivation is unverified.

components.text: 夕 is on the right; in the traditional account, it supplies the evening setting.
口 is on the left; in the traditional account, it contributes the speaking and name idea.
